trails.title: Fusion training
trails.subtitle: the store to the fusion head
trails.say: From the features-only store to a fusion head: the recipe names the head, every row becomes the 393 values it reads, the booster grows its trees, the candidate holds it, and promote moves it into live only behind the battery.

steps.title: The recipe names the head

entries.anchor: case "scratch": f = f.scratch(trees: trees ?? 500, eta: eta ?? 0.04)
entries.note: veilgarde train fusion declares the fusion head: a warm start of 80 trees by default, the flywheel's way to move the base, or a scratch fit of 500 trees, the way the shipped head was trained on 2026-10-21.
Plans the recipe and prints the plan, then trains it into a candidate unless --plan asked only for the plan.
Copies the parent bundle into a candidate, then trains the fusion head, the heads and the combiner in that order and verifies the candidate.

entries.anchor: let dataset = try FusionDataset.assemble(FeatureStore(directory: store), settings: f.settings)
entries.note: Assembles the store's rows, trains, and writes the head into the candidate with its parent's hash when it was warm-started.

steps.title: The store's rows become 393 values

entries.anchor: for column in layout.columns { x.append(contentsOf: selection.vector(column, row: i)) }
entries.note: Stacks each row's columns in the recipe's layout, the plain DINOv2 embedding and the nine capture values or both DINOv2 readings and capture, in id order, with the trainer's row weights, and marks the held-out new-generator rows and the evaluation twin's rows. A refit without the warp score lost 0.0012 AUC on held-out store rows on 2026-10-19.
The fusion row's two layouts: the plain DINOv2 embedding and capture, 393 columns, or both DINOv2 readings and capture, 777. A head's width names its layout, so a bundle of either kind runs.

steps.title: The booster grows the trees

entries.anchor: let twin = BoostTrainer.train(twinTraining, params: params, warmStart: warm, featureNames: []).model
entries.note: Fits an evaluation twin without a tenth of the rows and scores it on them, then fits the head on every training row. On 2026-10-21 the twin's AUC was 0.9817 on 11,212 held-out rows.

entries.anchor: let grown = grower.grow(id: model.trees.count, rows: rows, gradients: g, hessians: h)
entries.note: Grows each tree on the gradients the trees before it leave. A warm start begins from the parent's margins and appends trees, keeping the inherited trees' JSON verbatim.
entries.cite: test:integer features: xgboost's trees, node for node

entries.note: One tree, depth first: each node's best split by the histogram's gain, a leaf's weight from its gradients and hessians, scaled by the learning rate.

steps.title: The candidate holds the head

entries.note: Writes a trained model in its parent's place, hashes it and re-pins that slot in the manifest, so the candidate stays a complete bundle the detector can run.

entries.anchor: public func verify() throws { try ModelBundle.load(root).verify() }
entries.note: Re-hashes every artifact against the candidate's manifest; veilgarde route --bundle then runs the candidate as a whole detector.

steps.title: Promote moves it into live, behind the battery

entries.note: Moves one slot from a candidate into live: a snapshot first, the file written beside its target and renamed in, the manifest re-pinned, then the battery, and the snapshot restored on a failure.

entries.anchor: try check(slot, data: data, live: live, current: current, store: store)
entries.note: Loads the candidate's artifact for the slot and runs every check before live is touched, logging a refusal when one fails.

entries.anchor: guard let current else { throw VeilGardeFailure.data("the live bundle has no fusion head to continue") }
entries.note: Refuses a base that does not keep live's trees byte for byte, a combiner with a negative weight or a noiseprint term, and an atlas head that fails admission.
entries.cite: test:frozen and retired slots, a cold base and a blocking head are refused before live moves

entries.note: Runs the full detector on every image of every group the gate names; a hard group passes only at 100%, a ratchet only at its floor. Since 2026-10-21 two hard groups fail, so no base reaches live until one calls their four images right.

trails.title: Specialist training
trails.subtitle: the store to the heads and the combiner
trails.say: From the store's DINOv2 rows to the specialist heads and the combiner that pools them: each head is a logistic regression split by source and admitted only if calm real photos stay real, and the combiner is a bounded fit whose rescue is swept against the protect-real probes.

steps.title: Rows are chosen and split by source

entries.note: Trains one head of the recipe on the store's dino_norm column and writes its head.json, recipe and metrics into the candidate.
Keeps the usable rows, the head's positives and negatives and never a golden anchor, splits them by source, then standardizes and fits.
Holds out a quarter of the sources, drawn by CPython's own shuffle, so a retrained head is tested on the same sources the shipped one was.

steps.title: One logistic regression per head

entries.note: Centres and scales each of the 384 dimensions on the training rows only, with a constant dimension scaled by 1.

entries.anchor: cblas_dgemv(CblasRowMajor, CblasTrans, Int32(n), Int32(D), 1, xt, Int32(D), r, 1, 0, &g, 1)
entries.note: Newton's method on sklearn's objective, with Accelerate's BLAS for the gradient and Hessian, to within 1e-5 of sklearn's optimum.

steps.title: Admission: calm real photos stay real

entries.note: Counts the golden real anchors outside Bluesky that a head reads above 0.8. A head that blocks more than 10% of them is refused before it can reach the battery.

steps.title: The combiner pools the heads

entries.anchor: samples = try CombinerSample.captureAbsent(selection, base: base, heads: heads, pair: pair)
entries.note: Scores the store's capture-absent rows with the candidate's fusion head and heads, fits the combiner, and writes it in the shipped schema.

entries.anchor: heads: heads.map { Double($0.pAI(norm)) }, pair: pair.map { Double($0.pAI(norm)) })
entries.note: One row per capture-absent image: the base on its fusion row in the base's own layout, the three heads on its dino_norm, and an art-pair head's when the candidate trained one. The base is in-sample for a head trained on the same rows.

entries.anchor: let (rescue, sweep) = chooseRescue(w0: fit.w0, w: w, settings: settings)
entries.note: Fits the five weights with reals counted three times, then chooses the rescue weight by the sweep. On 2026-10-21 no candidate kept the top probe under 0.42, so the rescue took the fallback, 1.0.

entries.anchor: let theta = BoundedLogistic.fit(f: flat, y: labels.map(Double.init), m: m, sampleWeight: labels.map { $0 == 0 ? realsWeight : 1 })
entries.note: Zeroes the rescue column, counts each real row three times, and hands the rows to the bounded solver.
A projected Newton step under every weight at or above zero, so no evidence can be counted backwards.

entries.anchor: if real == settings.probes.count && top <= settings.maxProbe && chosen == 0 { chosen = candidate }
entries.note: Tries rescue weights 0, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0 and 1.3 and keeps the first under which every protect-real probe reads real and none above 0.42; with none, the fallback.

trails.title: Fusion inference
trails.subtitle: an image to the fusion base
trails.say: From an image to the base the stack builds on: the router picks the domain, the camera expert is the fusion head, DINOv2 and the capture signature make its 393 values, and its probability starts the route.

steps.title: The command hands the image to the detector

entries.anchor: let routed = try LensRuntime.withDevice(cpu: cpu) { try Detector.shared.detect(cgImage: cg, config: config, hint: domainHint) }
entries.note: veilgarde route decodes the image once and hands it to the detector, then prints the verdict, the base and the stack, or writes the schema-v3 JSON with --json.
The command line's one way to read an image.

entries.anchor: if let image = NSImage(contentsOf: url), let cg = image.cgImage(forProposedRect: nil, context: nil, hints: nil) { return cg }
entries.note: Decodes through NSImage first, then ImageIO: the pixels every shipped model was trained on. On rotated iPhone JPEGs the two paths differ.

Computes the shared signals once, picks the domain, runs that domain's base expert, then compounds the capture prior and the pooled specialists, the frame seam and the semantic chain in a fixed order.
A hint wins; otherwise the screenshot gate sends a flat UI to the screenshot domain and everything else to the camera domain. Routing is never by size.

steps.title: The camera expert is the fusion head

entries.note: The camera domain's base expert, and the fallback for any domain without its own.

entries.anchor: let p = head.predict(try vector(s, layout: FusionLayout.of(width: head.numFeatures)))
entries.note: Builds the row in the layout the head's width names, asks the head for P(AI) and labels it at 0.5 with a band of 0.04 either side.

entries.anchor: guard s.gate.isScreenshot, let sv = ScreenshotSpecialist.verdict(s.cgImage, config: s.config) else { return nil }
entries.note: A flat UI that reached the camera domain is read by the screenshot head instead, because a head trained on camera rows reads a screenshot as generated.

steps.title: DINOv2 and the capture signature make the row

entries.anchor: case .bothReadings: return try s.dinoFusion() + s.dinoNorm() + cap
entries.note: The row: DINOv2-small's plain 384 and the nine capture values, or both DINOv2 readings and capture, in the order the store keeps them. The second reading is the one the specialist heads read, cached in the signals.

entries.anchor: let e = try SemanticLens.fusionEmbedding(cgImage, variant: config.dinoVariant)
entries.note: The plain DINOv2 embedding, computed once per image and shared.
DINOv2-small's CLS embedding of the plain input, the one the fusion head was trained on.

entries.anchor: ctx.draw(cg, in: CGRect(x: -cropX, y: -cropY, width: sw, height: sh))
entries.note: Scales the short edge to 256, centre-crops 224 and normalizes by ImageNet's mean and deviation, drawn through CoreGraphics so row 0 is the image's top.
The frozen backbone's CLS token, in float32.
The nine capture values at native resolution, zeros when the image cannot be measured.

steps.title: The head's probability starts the route

entries.note: Loads the head's XGBoost JSON once into Frigate's evaluator and keeps it while the file is unchanged.

entries.anchor: stack = [SpecialistContribution(name: base.scorer, pAI: base.p, verdict: base.prediction, weight: 1.0)]
entries.note: The route's state begins at the base: its p and its label, and the first row of the stack.

trails.title: Specialist inference
trails.subtitle: the fusion base to the final verdict
trails.say: From the fusion base to the final verdict: a present capture signature first, then the specialist heads pooled by the combiner, the frame seam, the semantic chain with its preview tail, and the schema-v3 result the battery reads.

steps.title: Capture comes first

entries.anchor: let pooled = comb.pool(base: state.p, heads: hp, pairAI: pairAI)
entries.note: A valid, present capture signature suppresses every generated-side head. Otherwise the art, blur and human priors are pooled by the combiner onto the base.

steps.title: The heads read the force-resized embedding

entries.note: The art, blur and human priors, skipping any head the bundle lacks.
One head's P(AI) on the 360×640 embedding, a row in the stack whatever it reads.

entries.anchor: let e = try SemanticLens.normalizedEmbedding(cgImage, variant: config.dinoVariant)
entries.note: DINOv2 after the 360×640 force-resize, the embedding every head was trained on, computed once per image and shared.
A standardized logistic regression over the 384 values, the whole of a specialist head.

steps.title: The combiner pools the evidence

entries.anchor: if base < gateCeiling { z -= wRescue * max(0, -maxHeadLogit) }
entries.note: Adds each head's generated evidence to the capped base logit, and subtracts the consensus rescue only while the base sits under the gate ceiling. On 97,181 capture-absent store rows, taking the human push out moved 68 calls.

Caps each head's logit. The reference combiner also let an art-pair head lower the art logit; the shipped one does not ask, since taking it out moved 29 of 97,181 store calls, 19 of them to the right label.

A head's weight in the stack's rows: its generated push, or, while every head reads real under the gate, the shared rescue. Without the rescue a real wildlife photograph flipped to generated on 2026-10-19.

steps.title: A dark frame hiding the content

entries.note: When a real verdict hides a uniform dark border, runs the whole stack again on the interior and takes that evidence only when it is decisive. In the census it ran on 3 of 300 images and decided one, IMG_0500, a hard battery anchor.

entries.anchor: guard [imgTop, imgBottom, left, right].filter({ $0 }).count >= 2 else { return nil }
entries.note: Reads a 96×96 luma grid and calls a frame when at least two border bands are dark, uniform and darker than the interior.

steps.title: The semantic chain and the preview tail

entries.anchor: PreviewTail.apply(&probe, &state, s, capture: cap, semanticMajority: sm.majority, canDecide: canDecide)
entries.note: On the semantic-tile map and its majority: the preview tail, then the projection that commits a probe only under the production profile.
The semtile head on each of DINOv2's 256 patch tokens: a 16×16 map of P(AI) and the share of tokens above 0.5.

A small image read generated with a clean semantic vote flips to real only when the preview head and the live fusion head, its capture flags neutralized, both read it real. It fired once in the 2026-10-19 census, on a hard battery anchor's preview.
The fusion head asked again with the capture signature's validity flags set, so a small image's missing capture cannot read as generated.

steps.title: The final verdict

entries.anchor: InferenceResult(scorer: base.scorer, prediction: prediction, p: p, threshold: base.threshold, band: base.band,
entries.note: The routed result: the base expert's scorer, operating point and image size, the router's verdict, and the stack, the map and the trace around it.
Serializes the result as schema-v3 JSON with JSONSerialization and sorted keys, the bytes the goldens and the battery read.
Writes exactly the keys of schema v3, each block only when the result holds it.

trails.title: Watermark signing
trails.subtitle: an image to its signature, nothing added to it
trails.say: From an image to its watermark, with nothing added to its pixels: the native plane is cut into 32-pixel tiles, the warp residual gives each tile a fragility rate, each tile becomes four ordinal bits against its neighbours, sixteen tiles pack into a 64-bit word, and the words are named by their SHA-256.

steps.title: The command reads the image at its own size

entries.note: veilgarde watermark sign prints the signature as one line of vw1 text, or as JSON with --json, and names its grid, its bits and its id on stderr. Nothing is written into the image.
Signs an image with nothing added to its pixels: its tile codes at native resolution, read from the grid anchored at the top-left corner.

entries.anchor: let pixels = try ImageLoading.rgbPixels(cg, width: cg.width, height: cg.height)
entries.note: Reads the RGB plane once at its native size, with no cap and no padding. A crop must land on the same pixels in the same tiles as its source, and a resize would move every one.

steps.title: Every tile's fragility, by the warp residual

entries.anchor: let fr = WarpResidual.fragility(low: low, high: high)
entries.note: Measures every full tile's fragility rate from a given origin: each batch of tiles warped at both strengths, the residual read, the rate taken.
The forward and inverse tap tables for both strengths, built once per process: they are constants.
Builds the table pair for the weaker strength and the stronger one.
Moves a tile's four corners by the fixed displacements times the strength, and keeps the reference's inverse of the inverse for the way back, cast once from float64.
The 16 homographies as corner moves in [−1, 1], a literal table: every signature ever written was read through these warps.
The round trip through the 16 homographies and back, the error averaged over channels and trials, then a 9×9 Gaussian high-pass at σ 1.5.
A tile's fragility rate: how much more of it the stronger warp loses than the weaker, per unit of strength.

steps.title: Four ordinal bits a tile

entries.anchor: if v > g[nr, nc] { bits[r * g.cols + c] |= 1 << k }
entries.note: Turns each tile's fragility into four ordinal bits against its east, south, south-east and north-east neighbours, masking every comparison that leaves the image. An ordinal bit survives any monotone change of the residual's gain.
entries.cite: test:tile codes: four ordinal bits against E, S, SE, NE, masked at the edges

steps.title: Sixteen tiles make one 64-bit word

entries.note: A signature holds its version, 32-pixel tiles, 4-tile sections, the tile grid's rows and columns, and the packed words.
Four by four tiles, 128 pixels, pack into one 64-bit word in row-major order, with a mask word beside it. No hash folds them, so a bit that differs is one bit of distance, not a different word.

steps.title: The words name themselves

entries.note: The one line sign prints: vw1: and the binary in base64url.

entries.anchor: for w in codes { withUnsafeBytes(of: w.littleEndian) { d.append(contentsOf: $0) } }
entries.note: The binary: a magic, the version, the tile and section sizes, the grid's rows and columns, the section count, then every code word and every mask word, little-endian.
The id is the SHA-256 of exactly those bytes, so two signatures of the same pixels are the same id.

trails.title: Watermark matching
trails.subtitle: a crop or a re-encode to its place and score
trails.say: From an image and a signature to a match: the signature is read back and checked, the image's codes are read at sixteen grid phases, each phase slides over the signature at every whole-tile offset, the best agreement is the match, and the acceptance and the invariance run hold the signatures to their record.

steps.title: The command reads the image and the signature

entries.note: veilgarde watermark match prints the score, the bits it compared, the z-score and where the image sits on the signed one; --phases sets the grid phases.

entries.anchor: if trimmed.hasPrefix("vw1:") { return try WatermarkSignature(compact: trimmed) }
entries.note: Takes the signature as vw1 text, as a file holding the text, or as a file of JSON.

Refuses bytes that do not add up: a wrong magic, a length other than 20 bytes and 16 a section, a section count the grid does not have, or a version, tile or section size it does not know.

entries.note: The JSON form: the words as 16-digit hex, since a 64-bit number is not safe in every JSON reader, and a stated id that must be the words' own, so an edited signature is refused.

steps.title: The image is read at sixteen grid phases

entries.anchor: match(codes: try phaseCodes(cg, phases: options.phases), against: signature, options: options)
entries.note: Reads the image's codes at every phase, then matches them. The acceptance calls the two halves apart, so one crop's codes are matched against its own signature and a stranger's.

entries.anchor: public init(phases: [Int] = [0, 8, 16, 24], minimumBits: Int = 256, threshold: Double = 0.75, margin: Int = 1) {
entries.note: The defaults: a phase every 8 pixels, a match at 0.75 over at least 256 compared bits, and offsets that run one tile past every edge.

entries.anchor: out.append((px, py, TileCodeGrid(plane.fragility(originX: px, originY: py))))
entries.note: A crop starts at an arbitrary pixel, so its tiles straddle the signature's. Its codes are read from 16 origins, every 8 pixels in each direction, which puts one within 4 pixels of the signed grid.

entries.anchor: let region = array[originY..<(originY + rows * ts), originX..<(originX + cols * ts), 0...]
entries.note: The same measurement as signing, from a shifted origin: only the tiles that fit whole past it.

steps.title: Each phase slides over the signature

entries.anchor: guard let b = Matcher.best(crop: crop, stored: stored, margin: options.margin, minimumBits: options.minimumBits) else { continue }
entries.note: For each phase, asks the matcher for its best whole-tile offset, and keeps the best score over every phase, more compared bits breaking a tie.

entries.anchor: public var tileCodes: TileCodeGrid { Sectioning.unpack(codes: codes, masks: masks, rows: rows, cols: cols) }
entries.note: Unpacks the section words back into the tile grid, so the matcher compares tile against tile.
Slides the crop's codes over the signature's at every whole-tile offset and counts the disagreeing bits among those both sides measured; the offset with the best score wins.

steps.title: The best agreement is the match

entries.note: How far the score sits above chance, in coin-flip units for the bits compared. It does not replace the 0.75 floor: every crop that compared 256 bits scored at least 9.2 above chance, but strangers reached 11.9, since the matcher keeps the best of thousands of placements.

entries.anchor: public var pixelX: Int { offsetX * WarpConstants.tileSize - phaseX }
entries.note: Where the image's top-left corner sits on the signed image: the offset in tiles times 32, less the phase.
veilgarde watermark verify gives the same verdict as an exit code: 0 for a match, 1 for none.

steps.title: The acceptance and the invariance hold v1 to its record

entries.anchor: let report = try WatermarkAcceptance.run(sample.map { ($0.url, $0.label) }, settings: settings, note: note,
entries.note: veilgarde watermark accept samples final_mixed by a seed, half real and half generated, and writes each image's row as it is measured, so a long run that stops keeps what it measured.
Draws the same images from the same seed as the 2026-10-19 run did, each label shuffled by its own seeded generator.

entries.anchor: let cross = Watermark.match(codes: cropCodes, against: other, options: options)
entries.note: Signs every image, then measures each: a self-match, a crop of half its area at a random pixel offset, a JPEG at quality 0.75, the crop against the next image's signature, and on every fourth image the crop resized.
The share of ones at each bit position. On 198 images every position sat between 0.496 and 0.498, so no bit is close to a constant.

The kill criterion, fixed in code before the run: the crop must match with its offset in 60% of images, the median JPEG score must reach 0.75, and some threshold must reach 80% crop recall with at most 5% false matches. On 198 images v1 passed with 73.2%, 0.958, and 81.3% recall at 0.73 with no false match, on 2026-10-19 and again on 2026-10-21 after the residual moved.
Signs the battery's 105 images again and lists every way a signature departs from the recorded one. After the detection change and after the residual moved, all 105 were equal.
